action: General advice: enforce multi-factor authentication on file-sharing platforms, reset credentials after any unauthorised access and audit servers. No action needed for the public; services are unaffected.
exec: A national health ministry had a file-sharing platform accessed by an intruder, a reminder that auxiliary document systems are targets even when core databases are safe.
impact: Unauthorised access to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one Health Ministry facility; the ministry says the incident did not involve encryption of its main databases; health services unaffected. Amount of data accessed not stated.
plain: Malaysia's Health Ministry said someone broke into a file-sharing system at one of its facilities. Health services and treatment are continuing as normal.
summary: Malaysia's Health Ministry said on 14 November that it detected unauthorised access on 12 November to a supporting file storage and sharing platform at one of its facilities, and that the incident did not involve encryption of its main databases. It blocked public access, reset passwords, audited servers, enforced multi-factor authentication and is working with the National Cyber Security Agency (NACSA). The facility, attacker and data volume were not disclosed.
title: Malaysia Health Ministry reports unauthorised access to file-sharing platform

validation.note: The ministry's 14 November Facebook statement as carried by the Bernama wire (read 22 Nov; The Star and Malay Mail run the same Bernama text) and NST; not independent publishers, and the Facebook post itself was not read.

review.note: Compared with NST 14 Nov: incident 12 Nov, supporting file platform, no database encryption, containment measures
